questions.message: What was the LUCI flame spreading over in the fabric test?
questions.reference_answer: A strip of SIBAL, a cotton–fiberglass fabric.

questions.message: In the LUCI comparison the flame on which fabric lasted longer, the one in full gravity or simulated lunar gravity?
questions.reference_answer: The simulated lunar-gravity fabric flame lasted about 45 seconds longer.

questions.message: In the Saffire-II strip with Nomex attached to acrylic, which component actually burned?
questions.reference_answer: The upstream PMMA/acrylic burned. No Nomex ignition was observed.

questions.message: What does PMMA mean in the Saffire specimen description?
questions.reference_answer: PMMA means polymethyl methacrylate, or acrylic.

questions.message: What color change did the Saffire-II researchers see on the Nomex?
questions.reference_answer: They reported blackening of the fabric surface.

questions.message: What type of fuel droplet was used for FLEX-155?
questions.reference_answer: A free-floating liquid heptane droplet.

questions.message: What did the FLEX camera losing the visible flame tell the researchers directly?
questions.reference_answer: The luminous or hot flame was no longer visible. Later cool burning was still possible.

questions.message: Which two smoke-producing materials caused many missed ISS alarms in SAME?
questions.reference_answer: Kapton and Teflon smoke.

questions.message: What sort of detector on the ISS was evaluated in SAME?
questions.reference_answer: The ISS detector sensed light scattered by smoke particles.

questions.message: How was smoke produced in the SAME experiments?
questions.reference_answer: The investigators heated materials to produce smoke.

questions.message: Where was the 85% oxygen mixture supplied in the CFI-G inverse experiment?
questions.reference_answer: The burner stream carried it into the chamber.

questions.message: Which fuel gas was in the chamber in inverse ethane trials 21202A1 and A2?
questions.reference_answer: Ethane was present in the chamber.

questions.message: What happened after 21202A2 ignited?
questions.reference_answer: The flame self-extinguished about two seconds later.

questions.message: What two materials did the ICES comparison find shifted in opposite directions?
questions.reference_answer: P213 tape and polycarbonate.

questions.message: What spacecraft pressure was the P213 tape comparison conducted at?
questions.reference_answer: 8.2 psia.

questions.message: How many burns were planned in the 2026 FM² design?
questions.reference_answer: Four separate burns.

questions.message: Which fabric was selected for the four FM2 tests in the 2026 plan?
questions.reference_answer: Synergy Pro Navy fabric.

questions.message: Which four starting oxygen percentages are listed for FM2?
questions.reference_answer: 37%, 33%, 29% and 25% by volume.

questions.message: How does the FM2 apparatus set up the atmosphere for the next burn?
questions.reference_answer: It prepares a fresh atmosphere between burns.

questions.message: What shape was the PMMA specimen in the ISS study comparing diameters of acrylic?
questions.reference_answer: It was a cylindrical rod.

questions.message: For the LUCI fabric, how fast did the base advance in simulated lunar gravity and on Earth?
questions.reference_answer: Approximately 0.9 and 1.5 mm/s, respectively.

questions.message: How fast did the LUCI flame tip travel in the two gravity environments?
questions.reference_answer: About 1.1 mm/s in partial gravity and 2.8 mm/s at 1 g.

questions.message: How long did the aircraft comparison observe the SIBAL sample?
questions.reference_answer: Its window was twenty seconds.

questions.message: How big was the strip of SIBAL on the LUCI test?
questions.reference_answer: Approximately 5 cm wide and 30 cm long.

questions.message: How much of the downstream fabric in Saffire-II 2-7 blackened, and how much was damaged?
questions.reference_answer: About five centimetres blackened and the first centimetre was damaged.

questions.message: The Saffire row for 2-7 says 140 s. What was timed?
questions.reference_answer: It reports duration of the composite run. The Nomex did not burn for 140 seconds.

questions.message: What were the chamber oxygen fraction and concurrent flow in Saffire-II 2-7?
questions.reference_answer: About 22.1% oxygen and 20 cm/s.

questions.message: What size was the FLEX-155 droplet before burning and at visible extinction?
questions.reference_answer: 2.73 mm initially, then 2.52 mm.

questions.message: List the initial gas fractions for FLEX-155.
questions.reference_answer: 18% oxygen, 67% nitrogen and 15% carbon dioxide.

questions.message: Which instrument in FLEX-120 failed to provide images for the cool-flame diagnosis?
questions.reference_answer: The ultraviolet instrument supplied no images.

questions.message: How much Teflon smoke did the ISS detector miss in the published SAME test subset?
questions.reference_answer: It would miss two thirds of the Teflon tests.

questions.message: How often did Kapton smoke fall below the ISS threshold in the reported subset?
questions.reference_answer: Over half of the tested Kapton cases.

questions.message: What were the nominal oxygen mass flow rates for inverse tests A1 and A2 in CFI-G?
questions.reference_answer: 0.93 and 1.86 mg/s respectively.

questions.message: Between CFI-G 21202 A1 and A2, which trial failed hot ignition?
questions.reference_answer: A1 did not achieve hot ignition. A2 did ignite.
required_claim_patterns: a\s*1.{0,60}(no hot ignition|no ignition|did not|failed|didn.t)|(?:failed|no hot ignition).{0,40}a\s*1

questions.message: Which way did the P213 lunar oxygen extinction limit move versus the forced-flow extrapolation?
questions.reference_answer: It was lower than the WSTF 1-g extrapolation.

questions.message: Which way did the polycarbonate limit move relative to WSTF results?
questions.reference_answer: The lunar limit was above the WSTF comparison.

questions.message: What nominal pressure and tolerance does FM² specify?
What range of oxygen did the FM² researchers expect for the lunar limiting oxygen concentration?
questions.reference_answer: Their expected range was 24–26% oxygen.

questions.message: How many normalized observations and investigations contribute rows in the shipped archive?
questions.reference_answer: 1,058 observations from nine investigations.

questions.message: How many investigations and original experimental CSV tables are in the FIRST FIRE catalogue?
questions.reference_answer: Nineteen investigations and twenty CSV tables.

questions.message: The parabolic SIBAL result ends after 20 seconds with flame still visible. What duration can I infer from that run?
questions.reference_answer: Burning persisted to at least the end of observation. Exact extinction time is unknown.

questions.message: What changed in the LUCI atmosphere that complicates attributing the whole lifetime difference to gravity?
questions.reference_answer: Chamber oxygen fell from about 20% to 18% in flight, with two fuels sharing the chamber. The ground run stayed near 20%.

questions.message: I want to rerun LUCI to separate the atmosphere effect from fabric burning. Which measurements and controls should I add?
questions.reference_answer: Use a single fuel, comparable ignition and initial gas, synchronized oxygen and images, and follow burning through extinction.

questions.message: In Saffire-II sample 2-7, how can surface damage and zero fabric burn length both be true?
questions.reference_answer: Heating and possible deposited soot damage or darken the Nomex without evidence of sustained ignition.

questions.message: Can Saffire-II 2-7 establish that the same cloth would never burn when externally heated on Earth?
questions.reference_answer: No. Ground runs under external PMMA heating have supported burning of HT90-40 under different conditions.

questions.message: Name two observations after visible extinction that the FLEX-155 investigators used to infer cool burning.
questions.reference_answer: The diameter/vaporization history, its later plateau, and the cloud support the inference.

questions.message: Why is the vapor cloud in FLEX-120 insufficient to diagnose a cool flame?
questions.reference_answer: The cloud alone is ambiguous. The UV instrument supplied no images, leaving cool combustion unresolved.

questions.message: Could 155 and 120 isolate the causal effect of carbon dioxide on cool-flame persistence?
questions.reference_answer: No. Droplet support and pressure differed as well as the CO2 fraction.

questions.message: Would inspecting the SAME-R micrograph of Teflon sample 56 alone reveal if its alarm fired?
questions.reference_answer: No. Morphology does not give the sensor response relative to its alarm threshold.

questions.message: How would you test the relevance of SAME smoke findings for a ventilated habitat?
questions.reference_answer: Study size/material response alongside transport, threshold crossings and nuisance alarms under the target ventilation.

questions.message: Are the 85% CFI-G inverse rows suitable for filtering for an 85% cabin atmosphere? Explain.
questions.reference_answer: No. 85% describes oxygen in the burner feed. The chamber held a different ambient fuel mixture.

questions.message: Why can the A1/A2 oxygen mass-flow contrast only suggest a flow effect?
questions.reference_answer: Two observations with different flows and ignition outcomes cannot establish a causal flow effect without matched repeats or controls.

questions.message: Is the 2.3 percentage point polycarbonate shift in ICES Table 2 a measured change?
questions.reference_answer: It is a conservative extrapolation from a slope method, distinct from the signed material observation.

questions.message: What does the five-second ICES endpoint fail to establish about a specimen that remains alight at the end?
questions.reference_answer: It leaves later extinction uncertain. A longer observation could reveal delayed extinction.

questions.message: How does NASA Test 1 differ from the five-second ICES research endpoint?
questions.reference_answer: Test 1 uses five specimens and burn-length and flaming-debris criteria. ICES observed a five-second endpoint.

questions.message: Which outcomes should be kept apart when a bottom hot wire ignites an FM² strip?
questions.reference_answer: Ignition, sustained spread after the igniter switches off, and oxygen measured at extinction are distinct.

questions.message: NASA expects burn four not to ignite. Does that give us a NASA-issued numerical probability?
questions.reference_answer: The source gives a qualitative expectation. The guide supplies the illustrative numerical baseline.

questions.message: Under the teaching FM² threshold model with mean 26 and SD 1.5, what probability does 25% starting oxygen give?
questions.reference_answer: About 25.25% for sustained spread under the worked assumptions.

questions.message: If the FM² igniter is documented faulty, how should that burn be Brier scored?
questions.reference_answer: Mark it invalid/void and omit it from scoring, rather than assigning a negative outcome.

questions.message: Does nominal zero g in the NASA observation CSV certify the exact local acceleration for every run?
questions.reference_answer: It denotes an orbital microgravity category. It does not supply a measured acceleration history.

questions.message: LUCI flame spread was slower in lunar gravity. Quantitatively reconcile that with how long the fabric flame remained visible.
questions.reference_answer: Base speeds were about 0.9 vs 1.5 mm/s. The lower-gravity flame still reached extinction about 45 s later. Speed and lifetime are separate endpoints.

questions.message: A proposal cites the SIBAL aircraft test for the 45-second extinction difference. Which records should be cited for lifetime and for early base spread?
questions.reference_answer: LUCI and its ground comparison measured lifetime. The aircraft measured early base spread over a 20-second window.

questions.message: What combination of sample geometry and follow-up measurements would let Saffire-II inform a new lunar textile test?
questions.reference_answer: Match the HT90-40 grade, overlap, atmosphere and heat flux. Test continued spread after external heating ends.

questions.message: How do Figure 159 and Figure 124 change your interpretation of two FLEX entries both labeled Extinction?
questions.reference_answer: Figure 159 supports an inferred cool flame in 155. Figure 124 leaves 120 inconclusive.

questions.message: A classifier treats the 2.7 s entry for FLEX-155 as the last instant of all heat release. Identify the labeling error and a better observable.
questions.reference_answer: 2.7 seconds is associated with visible/hot extinction. Post-visible diagnostics such as droplet diameter, vaporization, or radiometry are needed.

questions.message: Would the fraction of missed ISS alarms in SAME give the time to alarm for my actual habitat, and which missing link matters?
questions.reference_answer: No. Smoke transport, layout, ventilation, filtration and installed sensing determine time to alarm.

questions.message: Compare the meaning of oxygen in CFI-G 21202A2 with starting oxygen in FM². Which of those belongs in a habitat atmosphere comparison?
questions.reference_answer: CFI-G 85% is a burner feed. The FM² values are planned chamber atmospheres. A gas flame cannot establish a textile rating.

questions.message: Place the P213 and polycarbonate ICES results on the correct sides of their respective Earth references. Name the two kinds of reference.
questions.reference_answer: P213 fell below a 1-g forced-flow extrapolation. Polycarbonate lay above WSTF measurements/data.

questions.message: Do the four FM² starting oxygen conditions form four independent observations of the teaching model’s uncertain threshold?
questions.reference_answer: They share the same uncertain limiting oxygen threshold. Treating their information as independent would double-count it.

questions.message: Using the default worked forecast, which single new oxygen test on the allowed grid has maximal information, and why?
questions.reference_answer: 26% gives the 50:50 split and one bit of information under the model.

questions.message: Does a NASA design expectation plus a SHA-256 digest establish that the team preregistered its own FM² prediction before outcomes?
questions.reference_answer: No. The digest alone does not establish external independent timing or team adoption.

questions.message: When comparing PMMA rods at around 21% oxygen, which common diameter lacks an actual near-21% orbital measurement?
questions.reference_answer: The smallest rod, 6.35 mm (often rounded 6.4), lacks a near-21% orbital point.

questions.message: A 1-mm rib on Saffire V propagated quickly. Is that a measured speed for a smooth ISS rod at 21% oxygen?
questions.reference_answer: No. Ribbed panel geometry and test conditions distinguish the panel from cylindrical rods.

questions.message: In the FLEX report, explain what could go wrong if a user joins rows by the test number alone for C03H401.
questions.reference_answer: The experimental table labels it 156 while the report uses 157. Match the engineering identifier and time, plus fuel/conditions.

questions.message: How would you determine whether CO2 affects invisible droplet combustion without relying only on flame photographs?
questions.reference_answer: Use matched droplet diameter, support and pressure, vary diluent, and combine diagnostic signals beyond visible images.

questions.message: Evaluate the statement that black Nomex and a dark FLEX camera frame both mean burning stopped at that instant.
questions.reference_answer: Saffire darkening is fabric damage/soot without fabric ignition. In FLEX visible disappearance can precede later cool burning.

questions.message: Explain one reason SAME smoke generation time and the CFI-G inverse self-extinction time cannot both serve as fire-detection times.
questions.reference_answer: A commanded heater duration generates smoke. The inverse value is a flame extinction event. Neither establishes an installed detector response time.

questions.message: What evidence would support transferring a five-second ICES extinction observation to an engineering material test?
questions.reference_answer: Longer observation, matched ignition history and local flow should be measured. Qualification also requires the standard’s specimen, burn length and debris criteria.

questions.message: The archive omits normalized entries for some investigations. Does zero rows establish that those experiments never took place?
questions.reference_answer: No. The catalog retains records where raw tables group settings or lie outside the normalization scope.

questions.message: Can the initial chamber oxygen alone tell us the oxygen at extinction in an FM² burn?
questions.reference_answer: The atmosphere can deplete during burning. A valid measurement at the extinction event is needed.

questions.message: Was it the visibly blackened part that burned?

history.content: Which trial placed acrylic beside Nomex?

questions.reference_answer: The PMMA strip burned. Nomex blackened without observed ignition.

questions.message: Did the other one have the same strength of evidence?

history.content: We are comparing FLEX-155 and FLEX-120. What did investigators infer for 155?
They found evidence compatible with later cool-flame burning.

questions.reference_answer: FLEX-120 was inconclusive despite a vapor cloud and missing UV images.

questions.message: Was the higher percentage in the air surrounding the burner or in its feed?

history.content: Let us focus on the 21202A1 and A2 inverse-flame pair in CFI-G.
We can compare the gas locations and the two trial outcomes.

questions.reference_answer: 85% oxygen was in the burner feed. The surrounding chamber contained ethane.

questions.message: What about the other material, measured against its own ground reference?

history.content: Contrast ICES P213 and polycarbonate, starting with the tape.
P213 was below the 1-g forced-flow extrapolation.

questions.reference_answer: Polycarbonate lay above the WSTF data.

questions.message: Okay, how much later was that event in the partial-gravity comparison?

history.content: I care about LUCI SIBAL extinction, rather than how fast the base moved.
We are comparing when the visible fabric flame went out.

questions.reference_answer: Fabric extinction came about 45 seconds later in the LUCI comparison.

questions.message: Actually switch to the ISS smoke detector. Which fluoropolymer did it often miss?

history.content: I have been looking at black acrylic rods.
The rod exercise compares opposed flame spread in orbit and on Earth.

questions.reference_answer: The SAME ISS light-scattering detector missed many Teflon tests.

questions.message: If its hot wire failed, would that count as a correctly predicted zero?

history.content: Let us discuss how to score the fourth planned FM2 textile burn.
Its outcome must be determined from an attributable observation.

questions.reference_answer: A faulty igniter makes the trial invalid or void. Exclude it when scoring.

questions.message: Now use the independent teaching distribution, what would its central 80% interval be?

history.content: In the FM2 worked example use a normal mean of 26 and standard deviation of 1.5.
That is the illustrative threshold distribution in the guide.

questions.reference_answer: With an assumed normal mean of 26 and spread of 1.5, it is approximately 24.08–27.92% oxygen.

questions.message: Using only the frozen research collection, what was the measured time to extinction on the lunar surface for FM² burn 4?
questions.reference_answer: The collection has no observed lunar outcome for burn 4.
